question: For each customer, calculate their daily balances for every day between their earliest and latest transaction dates, including days without transactions by carrying forward the previous day's balance. Treat any negative daily balances as zero. Then, for each month, determine the highest daily balance each customer had during that month. Finally, for each month, sum these maximum daily balances across all customers to obtain a monthly total.

WITH RECURSIVE customer_ranges AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        MIN(txn_date) as min_date,
        MAX(txn_date) as max_date
    FROM customer_transactions
    GROUP BY customer_id
),
customer_date_ranges AS (
    SELECT 
        cr.customer_id,
        cr.min_date,
        cr.max_date,
        cr.min_date::DATE as date_val
    FROM customer_ranges cr
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 
        cdr.customer_id,
        cr.min_date,
        cr.max_date,
        DATE_ADD(cdr.date_val, INTERVAL '1 day') as date_val
    FROM customer_date_ranges cdr, customer_ranges cr
    WHERE cdr.customer_id = cr.customer_id
      AND cdr.date_val < cr.max_date::DATE
),
cumulative_balances AS (
    SELECT 
        cdr.customer_id,
        cdr.date_val,
        SUM(
            CASE 
                WHEN (t.txn_date)::DATE <= cdr.date_val THEN t.txn_amount
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) as balance
    FROM customer_date_ranges cdr
    LEFT JOIN customer_transactions t ON cdr.customer_id = t.customer_id
    GROUP BY cdr.customer_id, cdr.date_val
),
daily_balances_final AS (
    SELECT 
        customer_id,
        date_val,
        CASE WHEN balance < 0 THEN 0 ELSE balance END as daily_balance
    FROM cumulative_balances
)
SELECT * FROM daily_balances_final WHERE customer_id = 1 ORDER BY date_val
